restrictions: Classical 256-bit word RAM; collision-frontier-v5 (C=1626 for sha3-256-r6).
Single-processor van Oorschot–Wiener distinguished-point search on f(x)=SHA3-256-r6(LE32(x)) with evaluation budget K0=1.10*2^128.
Success probability ≥0.39 under score-critical heuristic H-RF (random-function model for f on unevaluated points). Resource bounds unconditional.

Ordinary ops per evaluation claimed w=40 with visible spare above tight itemization (~35). Not zero-spare. Improves on awaiting-review unconditional 128.2465. Nominal 128 is not an established attack.
No classical 6-round SHA3-256 differential below birthday claimed; generic DP only.

heuristics.statement: Random-function model for the step map f(x)=SHA3-256-r6(32-byte little-endian encoding of x): whenever the algorithm evaluates f at a point not previously evaluated, the output is uniform on {0,1}^256 and independent of the algorithm coins and of all values observed so far. Used only to lower-bound success probability. Collision correctness and all time/memory/preprocessing bounds are unconditional.
heuristics.scope: Fixed six-round SHA3-256 prefix on 32-byte messages, iterated along DP chains from uniform random 256-bit starts, for the full attack with K0=1.10*2^128 evaluations.
heuristics.extrapolation: Truncated-n DP campaigns (n≤32) with k0_factor=1.10 are taken as supporting evidence that sha3-r6 orbits behave sufficiently like RF for contact/collision rates near the analytical curve at this inflated factor. Birthday-scale k0=0.9944 underperformed on sha3r6 truncated maps; K0 is therefore set to 1.10*2^128 (analytical RF success ≈0.45≫0.39).
heuristics.limitations: H-RF is unproven for six-round SHA3-256. Truncated experiments cannot prove n=256 behavior. RF-calibration at k0=0.9944 failed for sha3r6 (all n in {20,24,28,32} below 0.39); the claim relies on inflated K0=1.10*2^128 where sha3r6 n=32 (120 trials) achieved collision_rate 0.400. Exploratory lane only (plausible_not_refuted).
